промпт: Fields with a code or a number — each is a JSON object {"quote": the fragment of her words it stands on, copied letter for letter, "value": its value}; "quote" is a plain JSON string of her letters, with no quotation marks or backslashes of its own around them:

- occasion — what she does, not its frequency or venue: date is romantic, never inferred from company or venue alone. Unlisted ordinary social or leisure outings use everyday; event keeps her name. Working is work even at home (place home); studying is school, even daily; a hobby lesson is everyday, not work or theatre; someone else's wedding is wedding_guest, never celebration. The outing quote also gives movement when it says how she gets there, never movement alone; place where named; part_of_day when named; codes: everyday (Звичайний день), work (Робота), date (Побачення), celebration (Свято, вечірка), wedding_guest (Весілля, я гостя), mourning (Траур), formal_event (Офіційний захід), walk (Прогулянка), theatre (Театр, концерт), job_interview (Співбесіда), sport (Спорт, активність), home (Вдома), travel (Подорож), church (Церква), school (Школа), museum (Музей, виставка)

· travel — she is away on a trip or a holiday, and every outing of it, by day or in the evening, is travel; celebration — a festive event itself: a party, a birthday, an anniversary, a festive day. A trip or a holiday without such an event is never celebration
· wedding_guest — someone else's wedding, she is a guest, at any time of day
· sport — only when this outfit is for doing the sport (occasion_part sport); otherwise occasion is the kind of the selected part, never sport

- place — where she will be, also when only the phrase that names the event says it (occasion and place then stand on the same quote), and the place where what she names usually happens; a premiere at a theatre is theatre, opera_premiere only when her words name an opera. Her way to the outing and the street in her words about the weather are not where she will be: neither place nor place_words; codes: home (Вдома), park (Надворі: вулиця, парк, набережна), walk (Прогулянка), playground (Дитячий майданчик), cafe (Кафе), bar (Бар), restaurant_casual (Заклад: кафе, ресторан, бар), restaurant_upscale (Урочистий ресторан), fine_dining (Вишуканий ресторан), club (Клуб), house_party (Вечірка вдома), festive_dinner (Урочистий зал: банкет, весілля, вечірка), office (Офіс), office_corporate (Корпоративний офіс), office_creative (Креативний офіс), job_interview (Співбесіда), conference (Конференція), presentation (Презентація), theatre (Зал: театр, кіно, концерт, музей, конференція), opera_premiere (Опера, прем'єра), museum (Музей, виставка), vernissage (Вернісаж), school_parents_meeting (Школа, батьківські збори), hospital_visit (Лікарня, візит), long_transit (У дорозі: транспорт, переліт), flight (Переліт), sport (Спорт), church_service (Церква, служба), wedding (Весілля), funeral (Похорон)
· office_corporate | office_creative — kinds of one place, office: one of them only when her words say which kind; her words name only the office — office
- setting — indoors, outdoors or mixed; codes: indoor, outdoor, mixed
- duration_h — how many hours the event lasts; number

- movement — whether she will sit, stand, walk (her way there included), walk a lot, dance, kneel or do sport — also when sport is only one part of her day; codes: sit, stand, walk, walk_a_lot, dance, kneel, sport

- dress_code — the dress code, when it is named; codes: casual, smart_casual, dressy_casual, business_casual, semi_formal, festive, business_formal, cocktail, black_tie_optional, black_tie, creative_black_tie, white_tie
- palette — the palette scheme she chose for this outfit; codes: neutrals_plus_accent, tonal, analogous, muted_complementary, triad, color_block

- hour — start hour on a 24-hour clock, only when she names a clock time, in digits or in words; a part of the day alone (evening, morning, also with a weekday or a date) is part_of_day, never hour. "named": "clock_time" — you judge that her words name this hour on a clock; "quote" — only the words that name the hour, not the whole phrase with the date or the day; an hour without "named" is dropped; integer 0–23; {"quote": her words that name it, "value": its value, "named": "clock_time"}

- temperature_c — air temperature, °C, as a number, whenever she names the degrees — in digits or in words: «мінус N» → {"quote": "мінус N", "value": -N}, and «N градусів морозу» is -N too; «плюс N» → {"quote": "плюс N", "value": N}, and «N градусів тепла» is N too; named degrees always go here, and weather_feel then stays absent; number

- weather_feel — the weather in words, only when her words hold no number of degrees (a number of degrees, «мінус N» included, is temperature_c and never weather_feel): from her words, or when the season, month, holiday or place she names usually takes it (a summer month or a seaside place — hot; a winter month or a winter holiday — cold), with that word as quote; frost — she speaks of a hard frost, cold — of cold; codes: frost, cold, cool, warm, hot

- intent — what matters most to her (goal is a separate field with its own codes); her words about it are intent, also when they say how dressy the outing is (formality is then set besides): comfort_first — comfort and freedom of movement; context_optimal — being appropriate to the event and its level, also flawless or strictly by the occasion (with strict in goal_extra), also when she says it only through the judgement of others she wants to pass (that nobody finds fault with her look); statement — she wants to impress, stand out or be noticed, however she words it — then goal express is written too, on the same quote; conventional — none of these, also when she wants to be unnoticed; fashion_forward — deliberate bold fashion, including excess as a styling move, with at least two sources of interest; editorial — an editorial construction where count limits do not apply, with at least one source of interest; neither is inferred merely from wanting attention (statement); codes: conventional, fashion_forward, editorial, statement, comfort_first, context_optimal

- goal — how much attention she wants for this look — only its own codes, never an intent code: conceal — quiet, no attention to her look; flatter — usual, to suit her; express — noticeable, attention to her look: the words that give intent statement give goal express too. A body zone she wants to hide is goal_zones, not conceal. Passing the judgement of others is not conceal: it is intent context_optimal. Only on her words about attention to her look, never on her words about the outing itself and never as a default; codes: flatter, conceal, express

- goal_extra — what else matters to her in this look, several together: taller — a longer line, to look taller; comfort — moving comfortably all day; strict — strictly by the occasion; list (up to 3) of codes: taller, comfort, strict; {"quote": the fragment of her words, "value": [codes]}

- goal_zones — body zones she wants to draw the eye away from (to hide or slim a zone), with any goal: these zones stay quiet, the rest of the look follows goal. Never for how much skin she shows: that is open_zones; list (up to 3) of codes: belly, hips, bust, arms, legs, shoulders, neckline, back; {"quote": the fragment of her words, "value": [codes]}
- makeup — make-up for this outing; lips_hex only when she named a lip colour; {level — codes: nude, noticeable, bold; lips_hex — string #rrggbb}
- jewelry — jewellery she wants with this look; ethnic — wood, bone, beads; other — without metal; codes: gold, silver, pearls, ethnic, other, none

- registers — style registers she described herself with; list (up to 2) of codes: classic, minimalism, preppy, streetwear, workwear, sport_chic, romantic, boho, rock, quiet_luxury, gorpcore, dramatic, ukrainian_ethnic; {"quote": the fragment of her words, "value": [codes]}
- legs_above_cm — cm from the floor above which her legs stay covered; number

- month — the month of the event, only when her words name it: a date or a month, or a holiday that falls in one month — that month, with that word as quote; a weekday, «today», «tomorrow» or an event of any month — absent; codes: january, february, march, april, may, june, july, august, september, october, november, december

- occasion_part — which part of her day THIS outfit is for: the part she says it is for; when she has not said, the first part that is not sport, or the sport part when there is no other; a place alone never decides it. A clock time or morning/evening is not a different activity: yoga in the morning is still sport. other — that part is not sport; sport — that part is doing the sport; give it with occasion, with the quote of that selected part, not a quote of the whole day; unknown when you cannot tell; codes: sport, other
- activity — what she will do there; codes: children, rough_ground, stroll, walking, photoshoot
- surface — what is under her feet; codes: cobblestones, asphalt, parquet, carpet, grass, stairs

- precipitation — the precipitation she says the day brings, in any of her words (rain, drizzle, it pours, snow, wet snow), also in the phrase that names the degrees, with that word as quote; none when she says it stays dry; possible_rain when she says rain is only possible — not rain; codes: none, possible_rain, rain, sleet, downpour, snow

Items — lists of objects; every item she names goes into one of them, none is left out; each object has "quote" — the fragment of her words about this item, copied letter for letter — and only the attributes she named:

- wants — what she asks for in the look, and also an item she names as what she will wear on this outing when she does not call it hers — with every attribute she named, its fabric too; an item in her question («а якщо…», «чи піде…») is not a wish — it stays in question

- vetoes — what she does not want: limits. Whatever she wants the look without — an item, a feature, a pattern, a fabric, a colour — is a limit, also when she says it as a wish: written with the code of that very thing (without a pattern — that pattern's code, never the code of its opposite), with the part of the look when she names it; no code means «without», there is no wish with a negated code
- retract — wishes or limits from before that she now takes back
- beliefs — what, in her view, does not suit her or spoils her figure; never argued with

· slot — part of the look; codes: top, bottom, dress, set, outerwear, shoes, bag, scarf, headwear, belt, tights, socks, jewelry, earrings, collar_necklace, necklace, brooch, bracelet, ring, glasses, gloves, watch, swimwear, underwear, accessory

· item_type — item type; codes: evening_dress, cocktail_dress, suit, sheath_dress, sundress, blazer (блейзер), over_knee_boots, chelsea_boots, ugg_boots, ballet_flats, mules, espadrilles, pumps, dress_shoes, moccasins, loafers, sneakers, plimsolls, ankle_boots, boots, heeled_sandals, sandals, clutch, backpack, tote, baguette_bag, hobo_bag, crossbody_bag, bucket_bag, belt_bag, briefcase, saddle_bag, hoodie, sportswear, loungewear, leggings, jeans, t_shirt, shirt, blouse, knitwear, cardigan (кардиган), sweater, shorts, jumpsuit, skirt, trousers, coat (пальто), trench_coat, jacket (куртка), vest, top_garment, stole, kerchief, twilly, snood, shawl, bactus_scarf, ring, headband, bow, hair_clip, hair_tie, scarf_generic, jewelry_generic, bag_generic, dress_generic, two_piece_set, casual_suit, bodysuit, longsleeve, half_coat, down_jacket, fur_coat, sheepskin_coat, parka, raincoat, rain_cape, windbreaker, anorak, bomber, poncho, beanie, hat, beret, cap, belt, earrings, bracelet, necklace, collar_necklace, brooch, watch, glasses, gloves, tights, socks, swimsuit, lingerie

· fabric — fabric; codes: wool, cashmere, mohair, angora, alpaca, cotton, viscose, tencel, lyocell, modal, linen, silk, polyester, polyamide, nylon, acrylic, elastane, stretch, denim, satin, atlas, chiffon, muslin, batiste, tweed, boucle, corduroy, velvet, jersey, knitted, suede, faux_leather, leather, patent_leather, nubuck, velour, lace, guipure, openwork, woven
· pattern — pattern; codes: solid, polka_dot, floral, stripes, check, animal_print, camouflage, geometric, abstract, lace_motif, embroidery, print_generic
· color_class — colour class; codes: dark, light, bright, pastel, muted

· color_name — colour name; codes: black, white, grey, graphite, beige, cream, milky, sand, taupe, camel, latte, cocoa, brown, chocolate, red, burgundy, cherry, raspberry, brick, terracotta, ginger, coral, orange, peach, yellow, lemon, mustard, golden, khaki, olive, green, pine_green, mint, turquoise, petrol, light_blue, denim_blue, blue, navy, lilac, purple, plum, magenta, fuchsia, pink, rose, powder_pink, silvery, pearly, creamy, mocha, cappuccino, powder, soft_pink, emerald, electric_blue
· zone — body zone she keeps covered; codes: neckline, back, arms, shoulders, legs, belly
· feature — item feature; codes: heels, large_print
· length — item length; codes: mini, mid_thigh, knee, midi, maxi, waist

- own_items — her own items she names: everything she calls hers («моя», «у мене є», «з моєї шафи», the item in her photo) — each item separately, also when she sent a photo: objects with quote, name — the item in her words, status — has | maybe | not_wanted, slot, item_type, fabric — always, each a code her words give or unknown, and other attributes only when her words name them (not zone or feature), also for an item in her photo: the photo is looked at by another model. It is the only field for her items: there is no field per part of the look
Fields in her words — a string in her language, without quote:
- event — the event briefly: her own words from her message, in her language, shortened only by leaving words out; when she names several parts of her day, every part stays
- mood — the mood of the look, her words; list (up to 3) of a string in her language

- place_words — where she will be, 1–5 words for her scenario card, in her language, capitalised (like: Museum, opening; Country house, garden); whenever place is set, and never instead of it: the code of the place goes into place
- rest — whatever else her new message says that fits no field above, verbatim

- stylist_note — only when her words about the event are hard to read without context (a local custom, slang, irony, an event the stylist may not know, her role at the event, more than one event for the same look): one or two sentences in English for the stylist on what she means; the stylist gets her own words too. Otherwise unknown
- question — her question, her words
Fields without quote — the value alone, not {"quote", "value"}:
- formality — base step without evening; code lifts once by tier from part_of_day

· the ladder (step — its branches: clothes; whose standard puts an outing on the step; ordinary examples, not codes): home — loungewear, athleisure, sportswear; whose standard is only her own: nobody outside her household sees her, or the activity sets its own; e.g. at home, a workout, yoga, sport · everyday — jeans, a T-shirt and sneakers; neat casual, dark denim; whose standard is the street's: out among strangers, nobody she is with sets a standard; e.g. everyday errands, shopping, a walk, a walk in the park, a walk with her child, the playground, coffee with a friend at a cafe, a day of travel, a flight, a long transit · neat — business: a blouse, a shirt or a refined knit with trousers or a skirt, a textured jacket or a cardigan, loafers, ballet flats or ankle boots; whose standard is the usual one of her workplace or of the colleagues she joins as one of them; e.g. a work day at the office, a conference, a school parents' meeting | social: a day dress, a refined knit with a skirt or trousers, a textured jacket, neat flats or ankle boots; whose standard is the usual one of the place or the people she joins for her own leisure as one of them; e.g. a date at a restaurant, a theatre or a concert, a museum, a friend's birthday party, a house party · smart — business: a jacket with trousers or a skirt, a blouse or a shirt, loafers or pumps; a sheath dress with a jacket; whose standard is her workplace's, one step up because her look is judged there or she represents others; e.g. a job interview, a presentation, leading talks | social: a cocktail dress, heeled shoes; whose standard is the hosts' when they mark an occasion with a reception and she is a guest; e.g. a jubilee banquet, a holiday party in a restaurant hall · formal — business: a business suit — a jacket with trousers or a skirt of one fabric — with a blouse, pumps; whose standard is a strict dress code her workplace keeps; e.g. a workplace with a strict dress code | social: a formal dress of a noble fabric, heeled shoes; whose standard is protocol that the hosts or the place keep; e.g. a reception with protocol · very_smart — social: an evening gown; whose standard is only a written requirement for evening dress · ceremonial — social: a full-length evening gown with long gloves; whose standard is only the strictest written requirement

- formality_branch — the branch of that step, given by the same standard that puts the outing on it: business — her workplace, a job interview, a business meeting; social — a reception, a celebration, her leisure; only for a step of the ladder that has both; codes: business, social

- formality_reason — why the ladder puts her on this step: written — a named written dress code; norm — the usual standard of the place or people; evaluated — +1 because she is evaluated; representing — +1 because she represents others; her_words — her explicit wish. Give it with formality; codes: written, norm, evaluated, representing, her_words
- reserved_colour — a colour that belongs to another person at this event: near_white — white, ivory and cream belong to the bride when she is not the bride herself; codes: near_white

- open_zones — how many body zones (neckline or back, legs, shoulders) to show at this event if not one by day, two in the evening: none — church, funeral, interview, other reserved settings; one; two. Her own limit on what she shows (none, or one when she allows a single zone) sets it too and overrides the event's norm; codes: none, one, two

- part_of_day — part of the day she names or of her time (evening from 6 p.m.), also inside the phrase that names the event (said for one part of her day, it holds for the later parts until she names another), or when the event or a tile in "chosen" names it or usually takes it (an evening reception, a theatre, concert or opera, a holiday party held in the evening by custom — evening); an event that happens at any time of day — absent; codes: morning, day, evening, night
- minute — minutes of the start time, only when she names them with the hour (19:30 — 30; half past seven in the evening — 30); never without "hour"; integer 0–59
Advice topics — code: what to invite her to tell · when the topic applies (after your update, and only while the passport does not know it; for "advice_topics" the code has already checked it):

· an evening scene — part_of_day evening | night, or occasion date | celebration | wedding_guest, or place festive_dinner | theatre | restaurant_casual | restaurant_upscale | wedding | club | bar, or activity photoshoot
· outdoors — setting outdoor or mixed, or place park | long_transit
- occasion: ["Спорт, активність", "Подорож", "Звичайний день", "Побачення", "Театр, концерт", "Робота", "Свято, вечірка"] · she sent a photo of her item and no occasion, place or event is known

- goal: [{"label": "Тихо", "note": "Спокійні кольори, без блиску й відкритого — першими"}, {"label": "Звично", "note": "Кольори до твого обличчя"}, {"label": "Помітно", "note": "Хоча б одна річ тримає погляд"}, {"label": "Довша лінія", "note": "Колона в один тон, пояс на талії"}, {"label": "Зручно рухатись", "note": "Без високих підборів"}, {"label": "Строго за нагодою", "note": "Ошатність точно за рівнем події"}] · an evening scene

Required questions — code: what to ask · when it applies (after your update):
- occasion: where she is going: an occasion or a place · neither the passport nor "chosen" has occasion, place, dress_code or formality, and no event is known

- event_place: she named the event, but where it is and how dressy it is are unknown: ask exactly that and do not ask about the event again · the passport has an event, and neither it nor "chosen" has occasion, place, dress_code or formality
need — who answers her this turn:
- none — you answer her yourself: she told about her outing, or asked what you know for sure without her items, looks and photos — what a word or a style term means
- app — a question about this app — its screens, buttons, her saved data, what to do next: you answer it in your next message, from what the app shows

- look — her new message itself asks to judge her items or her look (how they look, whether they go together or suit her) or asks why a particular item or look was chosen: you answer it in your next message, after the app has checked her items and looks — only that check makes the answer sure. Telling about her outing, its weather and her wishes or limits for the look asks nothing: that is none
- build — she asks to put the looks together now: the app does it
